item.text: {"question_id":"3B.2","answer":"For the 2023 period, López Obrador demonstrably appointed, resourced, and directed an expanded security architecture centered on the military and National Guard: military institutions received most security spending, National Guard personnel grew substantially, and the Guard was overwhelmingly military in composition, although only 69% held the required police certificate (BATCH-0016-E007; BATCH-0031-E013). The framework contained meaningful preventive and disciplinary safeguards: required civilian-police, human-rights, and evidence training; formal duties prohibiting torture, disappearance, arbitrary detention, and disproportionate force; complaint escalation; written and reasoned disciplinary measures; hearings, defense, appeals, and possible administrative or criminal sanctions (BATCH-0055-E011; BATCH-0057-E014; BATCH-0057-E015). These are legal and capacity measures, not proof of effective enforcement. Operational performance was mixed or adverse: despite expansion, the National Guard accounted for only 0.8% of presentations to prosecutors and 1.5% of emergency calls in 2020–2023; its presentations fell 71.4%, confrontations rose 904.8%, and narcotics seizures fell 67.6% between 2019 and 2023 (BATCH-0016-E008). More importantly, independent and civil-society evidence describes widespread or recurring security-force risks during the period, including arbitrary detention, torture, excessive force, disappearances, alleged extrajudicial killings, incomplete detention registration, obstruction or weak investigation, and limited disciplinary referrals or sanctions (BATCH-0049-E011; BATCH-0003-E011; BATCH-0008-E008; BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0016-E005; BATCH-0016-E010). López Obrador’s policy-level responsibility is well supported through appointments, budgets, institutional expansion, and support for military control after the Supreme Court’s contrary ruling, but the supplied evidence does not establish his personal authorization of particular abuses or every decentralized incident (BATCH-0005-E001; BATCH-0031-E013). Overall, the record shows substantial formal safeguards and resourcing alongside a military-heavy command environment whose demonstrated prevention, accountability, and operational contribution were inadequate; it does not establish that abuse was uniformly ordered or
